sections.title: 0. Getting Started
sections.description: Essential plugins for newcomers. Learn what core features already provide before installing extra tools.
sections.intro:
#### First 30 Minutes (No Plugins Required) **1. Create one vault** and let it be messy — folders can come later.
**2. Turn on the core plugins you will actually use:** **Daily notes**, **Templates**, **Backlinks**, **Outgoing links**, **Bookmarks**, **File recovery**.
**3. Write 10 notes and link them with `[[ ]]`. Feel where the friction is.**
**4. Then return to this list and fix that specific friction.** #### Optional starting point The tool below is a general-purpose starting point: it pays off in almost any vault and does not lock your notes into a private format. It also appears in the job it belongs to further down — start here, then read that section before you install it.

sections.title: 1. Capture & Ingestion
sections.description: Streamline bringing external highlights, articles, academic citations, and media into your vault.
sections.outro: > The official **Web Clipper** and **Importer** cover one-off capture and migration; use these plugins for recurring pipelines.

sections.title: 2. Writing & Editing
sections.description: Enhance text input, table editing, formatting hygiene, autocompletion, and long-form focus.

sections.title: 3. Organizing & Metadata
sections.description: Structure your notes with folder notes, tag management, properties/frontmatter, and attachment rules.
sections.outro: > Keep canonical structure in plain frontmatter and core **Properties**; use these tools for editing ergonomics.

sections.title: 4. Linking & Discovery
sections.description: Find notes with fuzzy search, explore deep graph connections, and leverage semantic AI search.

sections.title: 5. Data Views
sections.description: Aggregate notes into dynamic queries, database tables, visual diagrams, and interactive canvases.
sections.outro: > **Bases** is the default starting point. Use for performance-heavy reactive views.

sections.title: 6. Tasks, Habits & Review
sections.description: Turn thoughts into action items, visual Kanban boards, time blocks, and spaced repetition flashcards.
sections.outro: > Pick one task and date convention; Tasks, TaskNotes, and Day Planner need compatible syntax to share a schedule.

sections.title: 7. Output & Publishing
sections.description: Share your knowledge through digital gardens, static websites, PDF/Word exports, and slide decks.
sections.outro: > Export tools need **Pandoc**; PDF output also needs a LaTeX engine.

sections.title: 8. Aesthetics & Interface
sections.description: Upgrade Obsidian with modern multi-column navigation, clean minimalism, and polished layouts.
sections.outro: > Prefer a CSS snippet for purely cosmetic changes.

sections.title: 9. Vault Maintenance & Sync
sections.description: Cross-platform synchronization, cloud backups, Git version control, and performance optimization.
sections.outro: > Use one sync mechanism per vault. Sync mirrors changes; keep a separate versioned backup.

sections.title: 10. Automation & AI
sections.description: Integrate LLMs, autonomous coding agents, and automated macros directly inside your vault.
sections.outro: > Before enabling AI, check what leaves the vault. Prefer local models for sensitive notes and versioned backups for agents that can write.

playbooks.title: Students & Learners
playbooks.description: Course material needs a reliable path from capture to understanding, memory, and review.
playbooks.intro: **Chain:** import slides and handouts -> annotate the source PDFs with **PDF++** -> sketch each hard concept as a **Mind Map** -> keep one **Periodic Notes** page per lecture week -> export assignments through **Pandoc Plugin** and proofread them with **LanguageTool**. Keep an inbox and a weekly review so the vault stays useful during exam season.

playbooks.title: Researchers & Graduate Students
playbooks.description: Make every conclusion traceable to its source while using AI to accelerate synthesis.
playbooks.intro: **Chain:** manage sources in Zotero -> pull metadata and citations with **Zotero Integration** and **Citations** -> annotate PDFs and EPUBs in **Annotator** -> recover text from scans and screenshots with **Text Extractor** -> keep frontmatter consistent with **Linter** -> plot results with **Charts**. Verify every citation against its source before you draft.

playbooks.title: Developers & Technical Authors
playbooks.description: Turn executable notes into reviewable, maintainable, publishable technical assets.
playbooks.intro: **Chain:** document decisions and commands as small notes -> style listings with **Code Styler** and draw flows with **Mermaid Tools** -> run shell jobs from **Terminal** -> paste references with **Auto Link Title** -> generate a **Table of Contents** for long documents. Treat generated text as a draft and keep tests beside examples.
playbooks.outro: > **Mermaid** diagrams and **Canvas** are core features — check them before adding a diagramming plugin. **Advanced URI** and **Local REST API** are what let scripts, Shortcuts, and agents drive your vault from outside.

playbooks.title: Writers & Content Creators
playbooks.description: Connect idea capture, long-form structure, media handling, and multi-channel publishing.
playbooks.intro: **Chain:** capture fragments on any device -> draft one file per chapter -> format as you type with **Easy Typing** and **Editing Toolbar** -> watch length in **Better Word Count** -> mark passages with **Highlightr** -> follow the structure in **Quiet Outline** -> resize media with **Image Converter** before you publish. Keep source notes separate from the publishable draft.
playbooks.outro: > **Readwise Official** requires a paid Readwise subscription. **Image Converter** rewrites files in place, so keep a backup before a bulk resize.

playbooks.title: Project Managers & Knowledge Workers
playbooks.description: Keep meetings, commitments, deadlines, and project status in one searchable system.
playbooks.intro: **Chain:** create consistent meeting notes with **Templater** -> parse dates with **Natural Language Dates** -> lay out milestones in **Kanban** and **Calendar** -> track delivery in **dotpm** and set **Reminder** nudges on commitments -> run a Friday review and archive decisions with links to the source meeting.
playbooks.outro: > A Notion-style database view is now core: start with **Bases** rather than a community plugin.

playbooks.title: Visual Thinkers & Designers
playbooks.description: Organize complex problems spatially first, then turn durable insights into reusable text.
playbooks.intro: **Chain:** diverge on **Advanced Canvas** -> turn the stable nodes into a structure you can navigate with **ExcaliBrain** -> make the vault scannable with **Iconize**, **Banners**, and **File Color** -> lay out reference pages with **Multi-Column Markdown**. Link every visual artifact to a decision or brief.
playbooks.outro: > **Excalidraw** also ships a community script library (flowcharts, palettes, import helpers) — enable it from the plugin's settings instead of installing another plugin.

playbooks.title: Language & Media Learners
playbooks.description: Capture, explain, and review vocabulary and expressions in authentic context.
playbooks.intro: **Chain:** watch or listen with **Media Extended** -> pull timestamped transcripts from **YTranscript** or **PodNotes** -> look up words in **Dictionary** -> keep the source page open beside your notes with **Custom Frames** -> import highlights from **Weread**. Revisit the exact clip whenever an example is difficult.

playbooks.title: Automation Builders & Power Users
playbooks.description: Use structured metadata and composable automation to turn Obsidian into a personal operations hub.
playbooks.intro: **Chain:** give notes interactive fields with **Meta Bind** -> bind repeatable actions to **Buttons** -> assemble dashboards in **make.md** -> find anything instantly with **Soma Search** -> let **Claudian** and **Smart Composer** work against that context. Start with one dashboard, measure friction, and add complexity only when it removes a real step.
playbooks.outro: > **make.md** is a heavy, opinionated rework of the interface — try it on a throwaway vault first. For sync, choose one mechanism per vault, never stack multiple sync plugins.

notes.themes: > 💡 Themes are installed via `Settings → Appearance → Themes → Manage`, and most expose knobs through **Style Settings**. Use the **Open** link to preview one, or browse everything in the official [theme gallery](https://community.obsidian.md/themes).
notes.templates: > ⚖️ **Warning about starter vaults:** they arrive pre-loaded with someone else's plugins and folder logic. Borrow the *ideas*, not necessarily the `.obsidian` folder — inherited configs are the hardest kind to debug.
